response.answer: Annotation hours: 1-2 hours per data point. Transformer fine-tuning GPU hours: 4-6 hours for 7B model. Cost: $100-500 per epoch.

results.title: Cost to Fine-Tune an LLM: GPU Hours, Cloud Pricing & Budget Guide | DeployBase
results.content: # Cost to Fine-Tune an LLM: GPU Hours, Cloud Pricing & Budget Guide. * GPU Hours by Model Size. 70B model fine-tuning ranges $100-500 per epoch. Fine-tuning cost = GPU hours required × hourly cloud pricing. Practical estimates: fine-tuning 1B tokens on 7B model takes 4-6 GPU hours on RTX 4090. ## GPU Hours by Model Size. * 4x A100: 40-80 GPU hours per epoch. * 4x H100: 25-40 GPU hours per epoch. * 8x H100: 15-25 GPU hours per epoch. Savings: $50 per fine-tuned 7B model using spot RTX 4090 instead of on-demand. Cost reduction: $8 total cost for 7B model on spot RTX 4090 with LoRA (2 hours × $0.34/hour). Cost reduction: Reduce RTX 4090 training from 40 hours to 20 hours by optimizing batch size from 4 to 1 with 4 accumulation steps. Validation fine-tuning costs $1-2 per model. Production fine-tuning costs $5-20 per model. ### Does model size linearly increase fine-tuning cost? Doubling model size increases GPU hours by 1.5-2x, not 2x.

results.title: GPU Hours Calculator: Estimate Your AI Training Budget | DeployBase
results.content: # GPU Hours Calculator: Estimate Your AI Training Budget. ## GPU Hours Calculator. 4 GPUs for 48 hours = 192 GPU hours. Cost = GPU hours × hourly rate + storage + egress. Use this to budget training projects. Gradient accumulation simulates larger batch sizes on smaller GPUs. Accumulating gradients over four steps quadruples effective batch size at the cost of longer training duration. Basic cost calculation multiplies GPU hours by hourly rate: Cost = GPU Hours \* Hourly Rate. Estimating GPU hours requires understanding training duration and GPU count. Distributed training across multiple GPUs adds communication overhead, increasing total GPU hours. Efficient distributed training adds only 5-10 percent overhead. Monitoring and operational overhead typically adds 5-10 percent to base compute costs. Training a 7B parameter language model on a 100B token dataset takes roughly 600-800 GPU hours on H100 GPUs. At $2.69 per hour, this costs $1,614-2,152. Training on four GPUs for one wall-clock hour consumes four GPU hours.
